THE GRADING QUESTION -- did wrapping in a sergeant Work add anything over just asking an agent directly?: Mixed, and mostly a wash for this one-shot single-stage case. Added value: a full replayable structured audit trail (journal + canned SQL analytics + doctor health checks) that a bare `claude -p >log.txt` would not give with the same query ergonomics. Added nothing to research quality or tool access -- the actor ran in a plain git worktree with identical filesystem/network access to a directly-invoked `claude -p --permission-mode bypassPermissions` in the same checkout; the 'primary source grounding in real repo files' came from cloning the repo, not from anything sergeant contributed. Net operator cost was real and disproportionate for a single question: clone a subject repo, hand-author an undocumented-in-practice sergeant.toml profile block, background the daemon with no lifecycle command, remember --profile isn't automatic, poll by hand, and manually retrieve the 'promoted' artifact before it could be lost in an ephemeral worktree. The one operational safety property this wrapping was supposed to buy over 'just ask directly' -- budget enforcement -- did not and structurally could not fire for this workflow shape.

friction_log: The predicted failure shape landed exactly as forecast: on this host/CLI (2.1.227, no post_turn_summary), a workflow explicitly designed for one-question-at-a-time human interaction cannot park in needs_input at all. GP-2 resurfaces as a hard product limitation, not a bug in this run — the `grilling` workflow is currently unusable interactively against the real backend on Cerberus. A first-time user running the promoted `grilling` workflow expecting a back-and-forth interview would instead get two rich, well-reasoned questions (each with the actor's own recommended answer) fired at them in under 90 seconds with the work already marked `completed` and the git worktree already torn down before they could type a response. There is no mechanism to answer question 1 after the fact through this workflow shape.

The only place the questions are visible to a human is buried inside `stage.detail` / `work.stage.detail` JSON fields — there is no first-class 'here is what the actor asked you' surface. A human polling with plain `sgt work list` (no --json) would see a wall of text mixed with JSON-ish payload structure rather than a clean transcript. There's no `sgt work transcript` or equivalent to read the actual conversation legibly; I had to reconstruct it from the raw blob store (`blobs/b3/<hash>`) referenced only by hex hash inside journal payloads.

There is no `sgt daemon stop` (or `sgt shutdown`) subcommand — the daemon top-level help lists daemon/status/run/work/respond/retry/cancel/analytics/web/doctor, and none of them stop a running background daemon. The daemon auto-spawned by `sgt run` had to be killed by raw PID (found via `pgrep -af`), which is exactly the kind of operation a first-time non-engineer user would not know to do or be comfortable doing. This is a real gap for a CLI that markets itself as having a self-managing daemon.

`sgt doctor` run before any daemon exists reports `[ok] daemon no daemon running; the next client command starts one` — reassuring, but it means there is no way to pre-flight-check 'is my permission_mode profile correct' without either starting a daemon or trusting doctor's own no-daemon-required read path (worked fine here, but it's not obvious from --help that doctor works with no daemon).

`sergeant.toml`'s shape (workspace/repository/profile/profile.options tables) is not discoverable from `sgt --help` or `sgt run --help` at all — it can only be found by reading prior run manifests or GAUNTLET history. A first-time user pointed only at the CLI would not know a config file is required, what it's named, or its schema; `doctor`'s 'no profiles declared' message (mentioned in the governing run manifest) is the only in-product hint, and only fires if you already thought to run doctor from inside the workspace.

Cost visibility during a live run is entirely journal-archaeology: there is no `sgt work cost <id>` or running total surfaced by `work show`/`status`. To honor the $4 budget cap I had to grep raw `usage.updated` events out of the journal ndjson file directly and sum `total_cost_usd` by hand. A real operator watching a budget would have no supported way to do this without reading internals.

Surface teardown is silent and immediate on `work.completed` — by the time I polled (~75s after submit) the git worktree was already gone (`surface.torn_down`, disposition `removed`). Any deliverable that depended on inspecting the live worktree (e.g., diffing uncommitted state) would already be lost by the time a human on a normal ~60-90s poll cadence looked. Only the branch ref (with zero new commits, since grilling never wrote files) survived by luck of git-worktree semantics, not by product design surfaced anywhere.

Positive note: the settle-driver behavior itself (autonomous `turn.ended` -> `stage.completed` -> next `stage.entered` with zero client commands) worked exactly as documented and was fast/reliable across two consecutive stages — this part of the product is solid. The gap is purely that the *workflow contract* (interview, one question at a time, wait for the human) has no way to express itself given this host's missing `post_turn_summary` affordance, and nothing in the run-time experience warns the user *before* they submit that the interactive discipline they're about to invoke cannot actually hold on this backend/host combination. A pre-submit capability check (e.g., `sgt run` warning 'ask capability not available on this backend; needs_input-dependent stages will run to completion without pausing') would have saved real confusion.

per_run.friction: Root cause of failure: cargo/rustc unresolvable on PATH inside the daemon-launched claude subprocess, despite CLAUDE.md opening with `cargo build` as the first command any session should run; the actor burned ~15 of its ~29 tool calls on PATH archaeology and then self-misdiagnosed the gap as 'cargo is being blocked by the permission layer' (profile was actually bypassPermissions) — a real correctness bug in the actor's self-report, not just friction. Compounding: gh issue view fails without -R on a locally-sourced clone; no sgt command scaffolds sergeant.toml (had to be reverse-engineered from a prior run's manifest); sgt doctor silently reports profile-less state with no hint when run outside the workspace dir; a read-only client command silently respawned a daemon the operator had just SIGTERM'd; zero usage.updated events were recorded for the interrupted turn despite ~29 real billable tool calls, so the $12 budget guard had literally no signal to act on. One material confound: the operator's own harness force-terminated the session at ~4.5 minutes, well inside the intended 50-minute observation window, so the run's brevity is partly an artifact of the observation setup, not only the product.

per_run.name: research
per_run.checkpoint_honesty: The single actor stage (00-investigate) was a real, judgment-bearing checkpoint in substance — the actor ran genuine first-party compression benchmarks against a real captured journal and made 7 WebFetch calls to primary sources rather than reciting known facts. But structurally the Work/journal/git-worktree apparatus around that one stage did no work a plain `claude -p` turn wouldn't also have done: the settle driver advanced turn.ended -> stage.completed -> work.completed with zero intervening client commands, so there was no decision point the durable-checkpoint machinery uniquely enabled. The checkpoint is honest in content; the wrapper around it is inert ceremony for a single-turn shape.
per_run.human_value: Deliverable quality is genuinely good and independently verifiable: it recommends zstd level 3, backs the recommendation with first-party benchmarks the actor ran itself (not just cited literature), cites 9 external primary sources (RFC 8878, RFC 1951, crates.io, NVD CVE-2024-3094 for supply-chain vetting of the chosen crate), and explicitly corrects the governing proposal's own '~10x' compression estimate down to a measured 6.5-7.7x — a real, load-bearing correction rather than restating the ask. On the narrower 'faster with plain claude-in-terminal' question the answer is yes: the operator's own comparison found the wrapping added a full audit trail but nothing to research quality or tool access (identical filesystem/network reach as a bare `claude -p --permission-mode bypassPermissions` in the same checkout), while costing real operator overhead (undocumented profile authoring, --profile omitted from the literal submit command, manual artifact rescue before teardown). Content: excellent. Wrapper-over-baseline: a wash at best for this single-shot shape.
per_run.friction: The literal given submit command omitted --profile despite the task's own setup requiring bypassPermissions — profile is not auto-selected from --backend; no `sgt profile list` exists so the only diagnostic is `doctor`, which only works from inside the workspace and reports a misleading 'no profiles declared' from anywhere else; no daemon-stop verb; the actor's own stage.detail claimed the declared output/README.md 'is not materialized' when the operator verified it was — the actor placed the deliverable in the wrong location relative to two competing conventions the package itself doesn't disambiguate; disposition:promote produced no actual promotion — teardown left the file as an untracked, uncommitted stray in a throwaway worktree and the operator had to manually `cp` it out before daemon teardown destroyed it; cost visibility arrived only at turn-end (coinciding with completion), so the run finished 7.8% over the stated cap with zero window to intervene, proving the budget guard has no teeth for this workflow shape.

per_run.name: grilling
per_run.checkpoint_honesty: The worst case of the three. Grilling's entire premise is a one-question-at-a-time human interview that pauses in needs_input between questions — that pause IS the durable checkpoint the package promises. On the measured host/CLI (no post_turn_summary), both stages ran to full completion autonomously in 80 seconds with zero stage.needs_input, zero work.needs_input, and zero respond commands anywhere in the 48-event journal. The checkpoint the workflow is named for cannot occur on this deployed backend — it is aspirational text in CONTEXT.md contradicted by measured runtime behavior, not a real durable boundary. This is pure ceremony around what functions as a single uninterruptible monologue.
per_run.human_value: The two generated questions (with the actor's own embedded recommended answers) read as reasonable, well-reasoned Socratic content — but the interaction model the workflow is supposed to deliver (real back-and-forth, a human actually choosing an answer) is entirely absent, and there is no mechanism to answer question 1 after the fact once the work completes and the worktree tears down. A human running plain claude-in-terminal would get a strictly better outcome for this exact use case: a real pause for real input. Judged against its own stated purpose, this run delivers negative value relative to the naive baseline, even though the text it produced is not bad in isolation.
per_run.friction: No first-class surface for reading what the actor asked — the questions are buried in stage.detail JSON with no `sgt work transcript` command, forcing raw blob-store hash decoding to reconstruct the conversation; no daemon-stop verb; sergeant.toml shape undiscoverable from any CLI surface; cost visibility required hand-grepping usage.updated out of the raw journal; teardown deleted the git worktree by the time a normal ~60-90s poll cadence would have looked, and nothing at submit time warns that the ask/needs_input capability this workflow depends on is unavailable on this backend — a first-time user gets no signal before running a workflow whose central discipline structurally cannot hold.

ladder_verdicts.argument: Cleanly clears §6.2/§6.4: bounded trigger (a topic needs investigating), bounded completion condition (one cited Markdown file), and genuine actor judgment (evaluate primary-source trust, decide what to cite, decide placement) that survives §6.3's reimplementation test — swap the harness and the checkpoint 'a cited findings file exists' still means the same thing. Correctly rung; the observed friction is product-maturity (profile discovery, promotion, budget visibility), not a classification error.

The package's own text folded its two extracted stages (snapshot, evaluate-liveness) into one actor stage only because A4's default rule forbids a workflow with zero judgment-bearing stages, not because the merged stage does much judgment: it interprets two already-deterministic readings into a busy/healthy label and stops — no mutation, no external side effect, and its trigger explicitly names dispatch's own embedded 80-monitor stage as an existing consumer. Standing up a full Work (durable journal entry, git worktree, branch, teardown lifecycle) for a strictly read-only 'print and interpret a snapshot' task is disproportionate machinery; this belongs as a helper/read command (`sgt-watch`-shaped) that an operator or another workflow's stage calls inline, not as an independently published, git-surfaced procedure.

The surviving stage (30-force-stop) gates a genuinely destructive, irreversible action (force-terminating workers) behind real judgment — confirm drain is active, require explicit --yes or dry-run, display exact identity before acting — exactly the §6.4 test (inspect evidence, choose among alternatives, explain a decision). The stakes (a destructive op) and the audit value of a durable, journaled record of who confirmed what and when justify the full Work apparatus, not just a helper invocation.

The sole stage absorbed five pipeline steps but kept the pipeline's only real judgment gate: inspecting a dry-run preview for secrets, duplicate entities, and unresolved outcomes before an irreversible external publish. A secret found here stops the run and only the source class (never the secret) is recorded — a genuine human/agent-in-the-loop safety gate ahead of a real external side effect (publishing a wiki page). This clears §6.2 and §6.4 on the strength of that one gate, even though five of the original six extracted stages were correctly demoted as boilerplate.

The package's own CONTEXT.md is explicit: 10-evaluate is kept 'not for a judgment reason' — it is a §6.5 deterministic-machinery candidate whose real justification is engine-gap G1 (periodic, processless re-evaluation with no billed turn), a categorical claim distinct from and stronger than the §6.3 reimplementation test. As shipped it is an actor-stage workflow only because the engine lacks a scheduler primitive; every invocation burns a full agent turn to answer a mechanical timestamp/status check. The owner needs to decide whether to build the scheduling primitive (making this a non-agentic engine capability) or accept indefinitely paying agent-turn cost for what its own authors call machinery, not judgment.

The surviving stage's judgment is real and consequential: deduplicating a finding against existing tracked work using an exact scoped marker (axis, source, finding ID, parent mission, branch — never a looser match), refusing a divergent stored body rather than overwriting it, and deciding whether the aggregate severity blocks a gate. This is genuine discretion with durable external side effects (tracked-work items, a blocking gate), clearing §6.2/§6.4 cleanly; the three folded stages (parse/sanitize, retain-artifact, route-each's mechanics) were correctly demoted as machinery around that one real decision.

The surviving stage gates an irreversible action (deleting worktrees and retiring task state) behind judgment that must distinguish 'verifiably not closed' from 'could not be checked,' re-verify ownership against deliberate spoofing vectors, and confirm handshake acknowledgement under a race-closing lock before any deletion. Destructive stakes plus genuine evidence-inspection judgment clear §6.2/§6.4; the six folded stages were correctly demoted, including one (background-watch) whose own extraction note already argued its own demotion.

The package's own 'Fixer note' is unusually candid: none of its four originally-extracted stages ever carried a §6.4 'Judgment required' heading — the whole procedure (enqueue, drain-and-retry, validate-acknowledgement, seal) is deterministic queue/retry/validation machinery with no discretionary actor decision anywhere, and the note states outright that confidence in even calling this a workflow is 'low' and it 'may not be a workflow with actor judgment at all, only a queue the engine should eventually own directly' (engine-gap G3). It was kept as an actor-stage workflow purely because the convention requires a materializable workflow to have at least one stage directory, not because the ladder actually classifies it there. The owner should treat this as an engine-gap finding, not ratify the current placement by leaving it published as a workflow.

engine_needs_ranked: Real-time and post-interruption cost visibility: usage.updated only posts on a turn's clean completion, so a canceled/interrupted turn (diagnose-bug) leaves $0 recorded despite real spend, and even a completing single-stage turn (research) reports total cost only at the moment it also completes — hit in all three runs and structurally defeats the documented budget-guard mechanism (cap breached 7.8% in research with zero window to intervene; zero signal at all for the interrupted diagnose-bug turn).

PATH/toolchain parity between the daemon-launched claude subprocess and the host environment: diagnose-bug's actor could not find cargo/rustc via its own Bash tool despite CLAUDE.md prescribing `cargo build` as step one, burned roughly half its tool budget on the resulting archaeology, and then self-misdiagnosed the gap as a permission block rather than an environment gap — a correctness bug in the actor's own reporting, not just friction, and one that would refight identically on every Rust-repo actor turn if the underlying cause is systemic.

Capability discovery gated at submission time, not just in doctor's static report: grilling's entire interview premise (pause in needs_input, wait for a real response) silently cannot hold on the measured host/CLI (no post_turn_summary), and nothing before or during submission warns the operator — a needs_input-dependent workflow should refuse or flag incompatibility with the resolved backend before it burns a turn producing a monologue it labels as a paused interview.

Daemon lifecycle verbs: no `sgt daemon stop`/`sgt stop` exists in any of the three runs, forcing every operator to kill by raw PID found via `pgrep`; diagnose-bug additionally hit a live daemon silently auto-respawning one minute after a deliberate SIGTERM merely because a read-only client command was issued against the same data dir — a 'STOP means stop' violation with real trust cost for a first-time operator.

Config/profile discoverability: sergeant.toml's shape, the fact --profile is a separate flag not implied by a matching profile name, and doctor's silent no-op outside the workspace directory were reverse-engineered from a prior run's manifest in every one of the three setups — none of the CLI's own --help or quickstart surfaces exposes this, a hard first-run blocker hit 3/3 times.

Layer-4 promotion/finalize is unimplemented: every one of the 8 single-stage packages declares a `promote` disposition in its output/README.md, but no finalize step actually executes the promotion — research's operator had to manually `cp` the deliverable out of the ephemeral worktree before teardown destroyed it. This affects all 8 packages identically by design, not just the one that was run.

Transcript/audit legibility: no `sgt work transcript` (or equivalent) exists; reading what an actor actually said or asked requires decoding raw content-addressed blob hashes out of journal payloads by hand — sharpest in grilling, where the deliverable itself (the two interview questions) was only recoverable this way.
owner_answer: The worry is partly right and partly not. The underlying idea is not broken: the research package, when it ran to completion, produced a genuinely good artifact — first-party benchmarks against a real captured journal, nine primary sources, and an explicit, correct downward revision of the governing proposal's own '~10x' compression estimate to a measured 6.5-7.7x. That is real, citable, usable output an agent produced with real judgment. But the library and runtime as they exist today are not yet something a human can pick up and trust unsupervised. Of the three packages actually exercised, one (diagnose-bug) produced literally nothing because a basic environment gap (cargo unresolvable on PATH) went undiagnosed for half the run's budget; one (grilling) is structurally broken on the deployed backend in a way that silently contradicts its own name and purpose; and even the success case (research) required so much undocumented manual setup, and returned so little unique value over a bare `claude -p` invocation in the same checkout, that the workflow wrapper was close to a wash. At the library level, the corpus's own internal adjudication process (A4) already collapsed roughly 30 of 34 packages down from multi-stage decompositions to single actor stages once tested against the ladder's own reimplementation criterion, and two of the eight sampled packages here (wake-and-resume, deliver-external-callback) go further and admit in their own text that they may not be agent-judgment workflows at all, just engine machinery wearing a workflow's clothes because the engine lacks a scheduler and a durable queue. That is a lot of decomposition, classification, and provenance-tracking rigor spent discovering — largely correctly, and with unusual self-honesty — that most of what got decomposed didn't need decomposing, while the handful of concrete product gaps that would actually make this usable (cost visibility, environment parity, capability checks before submission, daemon lifecycle, config discoverability, and finishing the promotion/finalize path) remain open and were hit in nearly every single dogfood run. The token spend bought a rigorous, self-critical map of what a workflow library should be; it has not yet bought a tool a human would reach for over just talking to claude directly.
